summary.text: A Poisson point process is a set of points randomly located on a space, with the essential feature that the points occur independently of one another.
The number of points in any bounded region is Poisson distributed, and the counts in disjoint regions are completely independent of each other.
On the real line, the gaps between consecutive points are exponential with mean 1/λ, which suits arrivals of customers, phone calls and earthquakes.

facts.label: Rate λ
facts.value: Average number of points per unit of length, area or time

facts.label: Where discovered
facts.value: Radioactive decay, telephone calls and actuarial science

facts.label: Homogeneous kind
facts.value: Has a constant rate, also called stationary

facts.label: In the plane
facts.value: Can place transmitters, particles or trees

items.prompt: Phone calls arrive at an exchange as a Poisson process of 2 per hour. What is the expected number in 3 hours?
items.explain: In an interval of length t, the number of points is Poisson with mean λt, so 2 × 3 = 6.

items.prompt: Customers arrive as a Poisson process. A busy hour from 9 to 10 tells you what about the number arriving from 11 to 12?

options.label: Nothing, as counts in disjoint intervals are independent
The count will be low, to make up for it
The count will be equally high, to match
The count will be exactly the same number

items.explain: The number of points in disjoint intervals are independent of each other.

items.prompt: In a Poisson process on a timeline, which distribution describes the time between two consecutive arrivals?

options.label: A normal distribution around the average gap
A uniform spread between zero and one
A fixed gap that never varies
An exponential distribution

items.explain: The distance between consecutive points is an exponential random variable with mean 1/λ.

items.prompt: An arrival has just happened in a Poisson process. Does that make another arrival come sooner or later than usual?

options.label: Sooner, because arrivals tend to bunch together
Later, because arrivals need time to recover
No effect, since the points have the memoryless property
Impossible to say, as nothing is known about it

items.explain: The existence of one point does not affect the probability of other points existing: the memoryless property.

items.prompt: Points are scattered over a region, but the average density of points depends on the location. What is such a process called?

options.label: An inhomogeneous Poisson point process
A homogeneous Poisson point process
A stationary Poisson point process
A fully constant Poisson point process

items.explain: When the average density depends on location, the process is called inhomogeneous or nonhomogeneous.

items.prompt: Which situation can a Poisson point process in the plane represent?

options.label: Days of the week in their fixed order
Locations of trees scattered in a forest
A single value that never changes
A list sorted from smallest to largest

items.explain: In the plane, a spatial Poisson process can represent the locations of scattered objects such as trees in a forest.
